items.title: "Side effects / stop signs: In practice, the most common problem is the "choline headache" ..."
items.where: Dopamine Receptor Burnout / DAWS Pattern: Uridine Monophosphate, P5
items.your_version: Side effects / stop signs: In practice, the most common problem is the "choline headache", or a spaced-out kind of brain fog. That isn't shown in the studies I've seen, but the likely reason is that UMP speeds up neuronal and synaptic membrane synthesis, which places a higher demand on choline than what people may normally get from diet alone. Other stop signs include insomnia, jitteriness, racing thoughts, irritability, emotional flatness, nausea, stomach cramps, or loose stools.

items.title: "Psychedelic caution: If UMP makes dreams vivid or suddenly lowers psychedelic tolerance ..."
items.where: Dopamine Receptor Burnout / DAWS Pattern: Uridine Monophosphate, P6
items.your_version: Vivid dreams and increased sensitivity to psychedelics are the hoped-for benefits of UMP. That means you should not take the old high doses of your psychedelic at first, as it might hit you way harder than you expected.
items.comment: idk where this safety warning came from, doesn't make much sense at all.
items.my_version: Psychedelic caution: If UMP makes dreams vivid or suddenly lowers psychedelic tolerance, treat that as a safety signal. Do not take UMP on psychedelic days. If you use psychedelics later, assume your previous dose may be too strong and that chasing the old visual threshold can overshoot.

items.title: "It makes more sense if there's also a genetic or clinical reason ..."
items.where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P, P1
items.your_version: Who this is for: 5-HTP is not for every depressed person either. It could help, though, with a low-serotonin-looking pattern, where it's hard to fall asleep and your mood is low, without much warmth to it. At night you get anxious and keep going over the same things. It makes more sense if there's also a genetic or clinical reason to suspect a bottleneck in serotonin synthesis, like with Scott, whose genetic data pointed to a TPH2 bottleneck, and 5-HTP helped his sleep and mood.  I'd avoid casually experimenting with 5-HTP if you're agitated or manic, as it could sometimes push that further. And watch out for serotonin syndrome risk if you're on serotonergic meds, or using serotonergic psychedelics/entactogens.

items.title: "The tool:5-HTP bypasses the tryptophan-to-5-HTP step ..."
items.where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P, P2
items.your_version: The tool: 5-HTP is a serotonin precursor, meaning your body uses it to make serotonin, which has been simplified online as the "feel happy neurotransmitter." People who respond to it can feel it quickly, because the mechanism is real, although it's not as strong as some hype it up to be for sleep or mood. 5-HTP has a lot of other functions in the brain and body as well, according to this broad review, including treatment of anxiety, myoclonus, obesity, but it carries a risk of serotonin-toxicity if levels go too high too fast, because it skips over the tryptophan conversion bottleneck.

items.title: "Scott's version: 100 mg 5-HTP sublingually at night ..."
items.where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P, P3
items.your_version: Scott took 100 mg 5-HTP sublingually at night, with 10–20 mg P5P sublingually in the morning. The P5P isn't there as a stimulant, but as the active form of vitamin B6, which the enzyme that turns 5-HTP into serotonin (aromatic amino-acid decarboxylase) needs. He's genetically slow-COMT, making him sensitive to too much P5P.

items.title: "Trial: Start lower if you are sensitive: 50 mg 5-HTP at night ..."
items.where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P, P4
items.your_version: If you're sensitive, start lower and do the trial with just 50mg 5-HTP at night for 2–3 nights, then go up to 100mg if 50mg was clearly helpful and not causing side effects. You can also add 10–20mg P5P in the morning, like Scott did, especially if the 5-HTP felt like it "almost worked," as that could be a sign it wasn't converting cleanly over to serotonin. Don't do the trial at the same time as the other suggested regimen changes (like UMP, agmatine, D-serine, psychedelics, or prescription medication changes), since the point is to see whether the 5-HTP itself is doing anything. If it's the right tool, the first things you'll usually notice are your mood or sleep quality improves, you have less nighttime rumination, and your dreams become more vivid or memorable
